questions.q: According to the summary, what comes first for anyone who wants to lead others well?
a: Becoming good at leading yourself
Mastering every technical skill in the field
Building a wide network of mentors
Learning to make quick decisions
questions.why: The first lesson says strong leaders organize their own lives and improvement as carefully as a team's.

questions.q: What question does the summary suggest asking yourself when fear holds you back?
a: Do I want what is ahead more than I fear it?
Have other people succeeded at this before?
Would failing here be visible to others?
Do I have enough experience to begin?
questions.why: If the answer is yes, the advice is to push through the fear and go for it.

questions.q: What did University of Texas research find about the way leaders speak?
a: They use the word I less often than non-leaders
They speak for longer stretches than non-leaders
They ask more questions than non-leaders
They avoid praise more often than non-leaders
questions.why: The summary cites this research to support the idea that leadership is not about you.

questions.q: What does the summary say damages morale more than any other managerial mistake?
a: Not communicating often or openly enough
Giving feedback that is too direct
Changing deadlines at short notice
Promoting the wrong team members
questions.why: A survey cited in the summary found under-communication to be the worst offender.

questions.q: Why does the summary advise never gossiping about colleagues?
a: It makes people assume you will talk about them too
It takes time away from planning and strategy
It makes you appear less authoritative to staff
It encourages employees to compete with each other
questions.why: The author says hearing someone gossip immediately costs them trust.
